pr_body:
Extends the attribute to apply to properties, and updates the source generator to support:
```C#
[GeneratedRegex("...")]
private static partial Regex Prop { get; }
```
in addition to the already supported:
```C#
[GeneratedRegex("...")]
private static partial Regex Method();
```

Closes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/77797

issue_context.title: Update GeneratedRegex to support partial properties
issue_context.body:
Partial properties are destined for support in C# 13.  When that happens, we should utilize them in the regex generator (we wanted this experience from the get-go).

This will entail:
- Updating `GeneratedRegexAttribute` to target properties:
```diff
-[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Method, AllowMultiple = false, Inherited = false)]
+[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Method | AttributeTargets.Property, AllowMultiple = false, Inherited = false)]
 public sealed class GeneratedRegexAttribute : Attribute
```

- Updating the generator to support instance and static get-only properties, e.g. if a user writes:
```C#
[GeneratedRegex("...")]
private partial Regex MyProp1 { get; }

[GeneratedRegex("...")]
public static partial Regex MyProp2 { get; }
```
the generator emits:
```C#
private partial global::System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex MyProp1 => global::System.Text.RegularExpressions.Generated.MyProp1_0.Instance;
public static partial global::System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex MyProp2 => global::System.Text.RegularExpressions.Generated.MyProp2_0.Instance;
```

We will only support get-only auto props. Others will result in an error diagnostic.

Issue Details
Partial properties are _possibly_ destined for support in C# 12. If/when that happens, we should utilize them in the regex generator (we wanted this experience from the get-go). This will entail: - Updating `GeneratedRegexAttribute` to target properties: ```diff -[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Method, AllowMultiple = false, Inherited = false)] +[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Method | AttributeTargets.Property, AllowMultiple = false, Inherited = false)] public sealed class GeneratedRegexAttribute : Attribute ``` - Updating the generator to support instance and static get-only properties, e.g. if a user writes: ```C# [GeneratedRegex("...")] private partial Regex MyProp1 { get; } [GeneratedRegex("...")] public static partial Regex MyProp2 { get; } ``` the generator emits: ```C# private partial global::System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex MyProp1 => global::System.Text.RegularExpressions.Generated.MyProp1_0.Instance; public static partial global::System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex MyProp2 => global::System.Text.RegularExpressions.Generated.MyProp2_0.Instance; ``` - Deciding if/how we want to support settable properties. (My default position would be to simply error on them, and only support get-only props.) - Erroring on non-auto-props with GeneratedRegex on them. This will all obviously be subject to whatever the design for partial properties ends up being.

Calling this out since it wasn't mentioned above as the things this would entail, but we should also consider at the time this gets added whether or not our Roslyn Analyzer and Code Fixers should suggest using the static partial method or the properties instead.

> whether or not our Roslyn Analyzer and Code Fixers should suggest using the static partial method or the properties instead

I think we should suggest the partial properties when we can; they are one parentheses pair easier to use than methods and the returned `Regex` is a cached singleton and matches the expectation that property accesses are cheap.
Moved this out since partial properties are not available yet.

review_comments: Does the source generator support both instance and static methods?

The value of `IPropertySymbol.NullableAnnotation` value does not take into account annotations deriving from attributes (`NotNullAttribute`, `MaybeNullAttribute`, etc) which need to be checked manually. We have helper code that does this in the STJ generator:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/59e8bbcf83b664c3de6cfa553d9bbfad76578765/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/gen/Helpers/RoslynExtensions.cs#L301-L383

but adding a suppression at the generated expression is the quickest way to get guaranteed results.

That should not be necessary or desirable here. The only reason the nullable information is relevant is for the generated partial to match the manually-written partial. For annotations, that's relevant, or else the compiler may warn that they differ. But for attributes, we actually wouldn't want to duplicate them, as all attributes from across all partial declarations are accumulated, and if we duplicated them, we'd get compilation failures due to multiples not being allowed. I've augmented the tests to confirm that.
